declared_exclusions.item: DATA CURRENCY -- my nine criteria are SILENT about whether the block's vintage is current, and would pass identically on a stale one
declared_exclusions.reason: Named on COO 68307's finding that an instruction can have two requirements while the criterion set scopes only one -- shipping the cot held-away exclusion alone would emit 449.7M with the exclusion correctly implemented, the served number still the one Andrew called wrong, and EVERY acceptance criterion passing. The same silence is in MY surface: AC2-AC8 verify the RENDER against the CONTRACT and say nothing about the block's as_of. A stale block renders faithfully, D1-inv-4 still closes (it closes against the block's OWN total_aua), and all nine rows still read PASS. NOT a defect in these cells -- data currency is the producer plane, not the render plane, and no D1 render cell scopes it. Stated so a certifier reading 'all 9 PASS' does not infer the DISPLAYED NUMBERS ARE RIGHT when what is proven is that the render faithfully reflects whatever the block carried. WHAT THE RENDERER DOES DO: it displays the block's own `as_of` on the invariant line, so the vintage is visible to a viewer rather than hidden. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: judge that vintage. A staleness verdict in a renderer would be both the monitoring reflex CLAUDE.md places under a standing moratorium and a trading-calendar false-alarm generator (NEVER#1) -- display the vintage, never adjudicate it.
